history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 364 / 'Bhagsunag Temple' (Bhagsu) - same temple. The Bhagsunath Temple stands in Bhagsu village, ~2-3 km above McLeod Ganj, and is dedicated to Lord Shiva and the serpent deity Bhagsunag. Local legend says King Bhagsu stole water from the sacred Nag Dal Lake, fought the Nag Devta, was defeated and then forgiven; the village (Bhagsu/Bhagsunag) is named for their reconciliation. The complex holds a sacred spring-fed kund (holy pond/jalkund) whose cold waters are believed to have healing properties, alongside a public pool fed by the same springs. Smaller shrines to Ganesha, Parvati, Hanuman and Kali Maa sit in the grounds. The temple is the starting point of the Bhagsu waterfall trek (waterfall ~1 km away).

name: Bhagsunath Temple
town: Bhagsu (near McLeod Ganj; CSV town 'Dharamshala' is the broader city, ~10 km away)
town_description: Bhagsu is a small village just above McLeod Ganj in the Kangra Valley, now within the Dharamshala urban area at the foot of the Dhauladhar range. It is best known for this temple, the Bhagsu waterfall and the 20-25 minute walk up from the McLeod Ganj market. Dharamshala itself - the Dalai Lama's seat and a major hill-station/pilgrimage base - sits ~10 km below; Kangra district is the largest district of Himachal Pradesh and holds most of its famous Shakti temples.

travel.road: Bhagsu Road runs from McLeod Ganj market to the temple (~2-3 km; 20-25 min walk or short taxi/auto ride). McLeod Ganj is ~10 km above Dharamshala on NH-503, connected by buses/taxis (verify).
